question_text: A 63-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his wife because she is concerned he is having another stroke. The patient says he woke up with right-sided facial weakness and drooping. Past medical history is significant for a recent case of shingles treated with acyclovir, and a stroke, diagnosed 10 years ago, from which he recovered with no residual functional deficits. On physical examination, there is weakness and drooping of the entire right side of the face. Sensation is intact. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following additional findings would also most likely be seen in this patient?

Question: A 63-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his wife because she is concerned he is having another stroke. The patient says he woke up with right-sided facial weakness and drooping. Past medical history is significant for a recent case of shingles treated with acyclovir, and a stroke, diagnosed 10 years ago, from which he recovered with no residual functional deficits. On physical examination, there is weakness and drooping of the entire right side of the face. Sensation is intact. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following additional findings would also most likely be seen in this patient?

Options:
opa. Decreased salivation
opb. Partial hearing loss
opc. Complete loss of taste to the tongue
opd. Wrinkled forehead
ope. Expressive aphasia

This condition typically results in weakness of the entire side of the face, including the forehead, due to lower motor neuron involvement. Bell's palsy can also affect other functions of the facial nerve, such as taste on the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, salivation, and hearing. However, complete loss of taste is unlikely as it would require additional cranial nerve involvement. Decreased salivation is a more common finding due to the involvement of the facial nerve, which innervates the submandibular and sublingual glands. Partial hearing loss can occur due to hyperacusis, as the stapedius muscle, which dampens sound, is innervated by the facial nerve. Expressive aphasia and a wrinkled forehead are not associated with Bell's palsy. Therefore, partial hearing loss is the most likely additional finding.",
